EngineEntry: The Sewers's play code starts here, from PhaseHandoff at $3FF3. It sets $AA to $FF, which lets the interrupt routine play the tune, relocates the scene pointers, clears the scene buffers, waits 25 ticks, reveals the status panel, draws the credits card, sets the background to black, waits for the death sprite's descent and goes into the main loop. Central Park's EngineEntry also sets $03CB to 1; this one leaves it alone.

ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch, The Sewers' version, called from MainTick every pass: it does nothing while $F8 is zero, and otherwise runs the trap or guard that the entrance rules at $8095 chose for the area. $F8 = 5 is the trap in area 4 (below), 6 the one in area 10 ($879B) and 7 the guard in area 14 ($87D5).

Area 4 ($F8 = 5). When the second actor has no animation ($63 is zero) and the player's X ($54) is from $30 up to $7F, it starts animation $B48D in the second actor's slot: frame 99 appears 98 across and 28 down from where the actor stands, drops 8 pixels at a time eleven times, and then frames 100 and 101 move it 4 left and 1 down a step, over and over. Once it has reached X 4 or less ($56) the actor is taken away: X, Y, $76 and its animation $63 are cleared, and the trap can start again. Every pass the player loses 2 energy (DamagePlayer) if they stand no more than 19 to its left or 6 to its right (the sum $56 + 6 - $54 is below 26) while its Y ($57) is $58 or more, unless the player's action, $6D with its two low bits cleared, is $0C.
no more than 19 to the left or 6 to the right?
has it come down far enough?

Area 10 ($F8 = 6). The actor that the entrance rules started with animation $B4DB (frames 102 to 104, moving 4 left and 1 down a step, over and over) is put back at the right of the area when it reaches X 4 or less: X and Y take the two bytes at $B4DE and $B4DF, which are the move of that animation's first step, $FF and $86. The player loses 2 energy if they stand within the same window across, 19 to its left to 6 to its right, and less than 16 above its Y less $48 ($57 - $48 - $55 below 16), unless their action ($6D with the low two bits cleared) is $0C.
near enough up or down?

Area 14 ($F8 = 7), the guard that the entrance rules started with animation $B505. If the player's projectile slot holds kind 7 ($0280), which is item 10 thrown once flag $03EB is set (SpawnProjectile at $9E31), with $0288 below 8, its Y ($0286) below $7A and its X ($0284) less than 32 to the right of the guard's ($56), the guard gets the animation $B55A (frames 110 to 127, ending on 127 held) and $F8 becomes 0, so nothing here runs again in this area.

Otherwise, if the player's X is at or past the guard's ($54 not below $56), the player's Y less $16 is less than the guard's Y ($57) and $02A9 is zero, it sets $B6 and $0234 to $FF: the latch DamagePlayer sets when the player's energy runs out, so the player dies.
has the player got past the guard?

AnimateWater, called from MainTick every pass where Central Park calls an RTS: the flowing water of The Sewers. Once six counts of the interrupt counter $E2 have passed since the time kept in $03E9 (the byte Central Park uses for item 17's flag), it keeps the new time and looks the current area up in the table at $8864 (sorted by area, so it stops at the first larger one). No wall in The Sewers carries command 30, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Event 12, which ends each of the guard's walking animations in area 14: chooses his next walk. His direction $03ED (a byte Central Park uses for item 21's flag) becomes $FF, right, when his X ($56) is below $3C, and 0, left, when it is $8E or more; between $4C and $7D it flips at random one time in four (NextPseudoRandomByte below $40). Then it puts the next animation straight into $62/$63: walking left, $B50A (frames 106 and 107) when the player is more than $30 to his left (counted from 8 left of him), and $B532 (frames 108 and 109) when the player is nearer or to his right; walking right, $B51E (106 and 107) when the player is that far to his left, and $B546 (108 and 109) otherwise. Each step moves him 4 across and 1 up or down, and each animation ends with event 12 again.

The scene list DrawUiImageRecord points $02/$03 at for a panel picture, as Central Park's: one record, $00 $0E $0E, whose third byte has bits 5 and 6 clear, so no colour swap bytes follow, and the $FF that ends the list.

The second scene list, for item 10's picture once flag $03EB is set: the record $00 $0E $4E, whose third byte has bit 6 set, so two colour swap bytes follow: $21 (white, 1, becomes red, 2) and $2F (light grey, 15, becomes red). Then the $FF that ends the list.
Rows 3 and 9, one for each of the panel's two boxes: DrawUiImageRecord reads the row for the box in X here and draws the picture at column 33 of it.

Purpose: dissolve and erase the display strip at $0C00-$0FFF. Inputs: current strip contents and pseudo-random state. Outputs: several masked dissolve passes are displayed and the region is finally cleared. Assumptions: the range is the intended visible region under the current VIC-II layout. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and random and delay scratch. Hardware changes: changes hardware-visible bitmap or screen RAM; no direct VIC-II register write.

The masks $3F, $CF, $F3 and $FC, each clearing one of the four two-bit pixels of a multicolour byte: the dissolve at $9BA1 takes a random number from 0 to 3 for each byte of the strip and ANDs that mask into it, so the picture crumbles a pixel at a time.

Purpose: Advance and return The Sewers's table- and CIA-timer-mixed pseudo-random byte. Inputs: $F9/$FA is the readable table pointer, $FB is the previous random byte, Y is caller state to preserve, and CIA 1 Timer A is running at $DC04/$DC05. Outputs: If old $FA is at least $B6, sets $FA=($DC04 & $1F)+$75 and $F9=$DC05. Then A and $FB receive old $FB + byte[$F9/$FA] + $DC04 modulo 256; $F9 increments and $FA increments on low-byte wrap; Y is restored. Assumptions: $F9/$FA points at readable mapped data. Both paths establish carry clear before the two ADC operations, and the caller accepts CIA-timer-dependent output. Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, V, and $F9-$FB; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: Reads CIA 1 Timer A low byte $DC04 on every call and high byte $DC05 only on reseed; performs no hardware write.

Subtract unsigned A from player health $0229 with saturation at zero. Positive remaining health preserves action $6D and death latch $B6. Only the zero-result path sets $6D=($69>>1)+$24 and $B6=$FF. X/Y are preserved; no hardware registers are written. Live tests cover positive, equal, excessive and zero damage, including health 0 and 255.

Purpose: subtract one hit from enemy health, update its HUD value, and on defeat persist position/time state and award score
Inputs: A = unsigned damage; enemy health $022A; current area $A2; enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B; tick/time state; defeated-count limit $D6
Outputs: stores saturated health in $022A and HUD cell $3F92,$A2; on defeat awards score, records position/heading/time in $013F/$0151/$0163/$0175/$0187 indexed by area, advances bounded persistent state $012D,X, and installs reaction/action $24
Assumptions: area-indexed persistent arrays and resident score helper are valid
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and score/persistence/reaction scratch
Hardware changes: none directly; HUD and score display state change through RAM/helpers

Purpose: create the current area's enemy from static spawn tables or restore its persistent defeated/position record
Inputs: area index $A2; spawn/profile tables $9DC0,$9DD2,$9DE4,$9DF6,$9E08; persistent state $012D/$013F/$0151/$0163; related enemy profile fields
Outputs: initializes enemy script/motion, extents, delay, AI state, type/attributes, position, heading, action and timing fields; a zero spawn Y disables the enemy; otherwise composes its initial logical sprites
Assumptions: area indexes all parallel tables and negative $012D,X denotes the persistent restore path

Eight pose entries read at $9D8B. Y is half the selected enemy heading on the ordinary path and an adjusted heading on the preserved-enemy path; result goes to $67. The table is separate from the area-indexed enemy fields.

Eight mirror/auxiliary flags read at $9D90 using the same heading-derived Y as $9DB0; writes $5F. Values are zero or $FF; the exact visual effect is traced by the frame composer, not inferred from the flag name.
18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9DC0-$9DD1: the enemy's kind in the high nibble and its profile in the low nibble. Values: 0, 32, 97, 98, 0, 0, 99, 129, 0, 130, 0, 195, 33, 193, 0, 0, 0, 0.

18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9DE4-$9DF5: the Y position it starts at; 0 means the area has no enemy. Values: 0, 102, 110, 117, 0, 0, 108, 137, 0, 115, 0, 83, 93, 89, 0, 0, 0, 0.

18 bytes, one for each area by number, $9DF6-$9E07: its heading in the low three bits and its weapon in the high nibble. Values: 65, 69, 67, 69, 65, 65, 71, 69, 65, 67, 65, 69, 71, 69, 65, 65, 65, 65.

Purpose: spawn the attacking actor's projectile into its fixed player or enemy slot after the combat-overlap precheck
Inputs: X = source actor offset (0 player, nonzero enemy); actor position/facing $54-$57/$69/$6B; player selected-object state $70/$0279/$03DC; projectile arrays $0280-$0289
Outputs: player attacks populate slot 0 only when free and allowed by selected-object state; enemy attacks populate slot 1; position, direction, lifetime, and collision stamps are initialized
Assumptions: two projectile slots are encoded at adjacent indices and actor coordinates/headings are initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and combat-overlap/projectile initialization scratch
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: initialize the single projectile slot when it is free. Inputs: A is projectile kind or state and actor and facing context are valid. Outputs: projectile owner, direction, coordinates, and state are initialized or left unchanged when occupied. Assumptions: the engine uses one active projectile slot. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and projectile state. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: test a projectile/actor pair against the engine's two-axis collision box. Inputs: X selects projectile coordinates $0284,X/$0286,X; Y selects actor coordinates $54,Y/$55,Y. Outputs: carry is clear exactly when absolute vertical distance is below 8 and absolute horizontal distance is below 6; carry is set on either rejection. Assumptions: the caller consumes carry immediately and X/Y select valid slots. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: initialize a projectile trajectory from an actor. Inputs: projectile type, source actor, facing, and coordinates. Outputs: projectile owner, state, origin, direction, and signed velocity are installed. Assumptions: the projectile slot has already been accepted. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and projectile state. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: advance both projectile slots for elapsed IRQ ticks and remove or resolve projectiles that expire, leave bounds, hit geometry, or overlap an actor
Inputs: tick $E2/$0273; two projectile slots in $0280-$0289; compiled collision geometry and actor positions/extents/health
Outputs: stamps elapsed delta in $8F/$0273; advances lifetime and coordinates for slots 1 then 0; clears expired/hit slots and applies damage/reaction on actor overlap
Assumptions: IRQ tick advances, projectile arrays use the verified adjacent-slot layout, and collision/actor state is initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and projectile, collision, overlap, damage, and reaction scratch
Hardware changes: none directly; updates logical state rendered later

Sixteen bytes, one for each projectile state (the kind in the low three bits; bit 3, which the drawing routine flips every time it draws, gives the second picture): with a high byte at +16 that is not zero, the low byte of the address of an unpacked picture, otherwise the number of the packed sprite to draw. By state: sprite 0, sprite 74, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, sprite 74, sprite 74, sprite 0, sprite 75, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, $EBB2, sprite 75, sprite 75.
The high bytes of the same sixteen pictures; 0 means the low byte is a packed sprite number.
Fifteen sprite attribute bytes by projectile state, copied to the sprite slot's $0220 entry when it is drawn: -1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, 0, -1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 6.
X offsets from the projectile's position to where its sprite is drawn, by kind (the state's low three bits): 2, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 4. The eighth is also the first Y offset.
Y offsets for drawing, by kind, read from here with the same index: 4, 12, 0, 0, 0, 0, 12, 12; the eighth is the first launch offset.

Where a projectile appears beside whoever throws it, by the thrower's heading h: the X offset is the byte at $A068+h and the Y offset the one after it, so the eight headings share nine bytes: 12, 18, -2, 18, 0, -8, 0, -8, -2. A launch whose X position would wrap past 0 or 255 is cancelled.
Projectile launch offsets plus 1, the address the instructions at $9E99 and $9EEB read with X as the index: the table read from its byte 1 on.

How far a flying projectile moves each step, as X and Y pairs overlapping in the same way: X at $A070+i and Y at the byte after, where i is its heading plus the offset for its kind at $A089; the furthest index reads into that table. Values: -2, 4, -1, 4, 1, -4, 1, -4, -1, 4, 0, 4, 2, -4, 2, -4, 0, 2, 2, 1, 2, -2, 2, 4, 2.
Projectile motion steps plus 1, the address the instruction at $9F9F reads with Y as the index: the table read from its byte 1 on.
The offset into the motion steps for each of the eight kinds: 0, 0, 20, 14, 16, 18, 8, 8. Kinds that share an offset fly the same way.

Purpose: expand the current area's encoded collision list into fixed six-byte segment records for movement tests
Inputs: area index $A2; concatenated $FF-terminated source lists beginning at $8593; line/slope parameters consumed by the compiler and Multiply
Outputs: emits endpoint, gradient, flags, and optional-action fields as six-byte records beginning at $F2CB and writes a zero terminator at the next record
Assumptions: $A2 identifies an existing terminated list and enough RAM is available from $F2CB upward
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and collision-compiler arithmetic/pointer scratch
Hardware changes: none; writes RAM beneath the KERNAL region under the game's all-RAM banking model

Purpose: compute an unsigned 8-by-8-bit product for collision arithmetic
Inputs: X = unsigned multiplicand; Y = unsigned multiplier
Outputs: Y:X = 16-bit unsigned product
Assumptions: ordinary NMOS 6502 shift/add arithmetic and scratch $45-$47 are available
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and $45-$47
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: test the candidate movement segment against every compiled collision record and report collision plus any encoded trigger
Inputs: X = heading/direction selector; old and candidate coordinates $48-$4B; movement profile $027F; six-byte records beginning at $F2CB
Outputs: returns A=$FF for collision or A=0 for none and restores X from $F3; records the matched record offset in $24; an eligible special segment may set action $80 and OR trigger/collision state into $81
Assumptions: the compiled table is zero-terminated and each nonzero record has the verified six-byte layout
Clobbers: A, Y, flags and collision arithmetic scratch including $23/$24,$45-$47,$F3; X is restored on return
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: invoke sprite composition in the requested masked or collision mode. Inputs: A is mode plus the named compositor's normal actor and frame context. Outputs: composite sprite buffers and metadata are produced. Assumptions: the shared compositor inputs are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and extensive compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Purpose: decode one actor frame descriptor into positioned logical sprite components, temporarily exposing RAM beneath KERNAL for high-memory source data
Inputs: A = frame attribute/modifier; Y = frame-descriptor index; X = first logical-sprite slot; actor state including $70,$72,$7D and frame pointer tables at $AB6C
Outputs: writes component bitmap references, positions, flags, and ready state into logical sprite arrays $0200-$0258 and sets sprite-dirty state as required
Assumptions: frame pointers/descriptors are valid and the caller enters with the normal $01 banking value expected by the matching INC restoration
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and sprite-composition scratch including $F1,$92,$9F
Hardware changes: decrements then restores CPU port $01 to expose high RAM transiently; does not directly write VIC-II sprite registers
Never reached: the instruction before ends with JMP, and no instruction, branch or pointer in this load names this address.

Purpose: Enter The Sewers playable phase's common sprite-composition body with the mode already prepared by the masked-mode caller.
Inputs: A/$F1 and $92 contain the prepared composition mode; X selects the logical sprite group; Y selects the frame descriptor; CPU port $01 is in the engine's normal I/O-visible state.
Outputs: Decrements $01 for the required high-memory RAM visibility, resolves and composes the selected frame into logical sprite work buffers, restores $01 before return, and records composition state.
Assumptions: The frame descriptor and phase sprite tables are valid; the routine's balanced DEC/INC of $01 is not interrupted by an alternate exit.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $02/$03, $92/$97/$9F, $F1, and logical sprite work buffers.
Hardware changes: Changes CPU-port $01 transiently by one decrement and a balancing increment to expose the required high-memory RAM; writes sprite work buffers, not VIC-II registers directly.

Purpose: Finish The Sewers playable phase's empty composite-sprite slot by marking its descriptor and restoring CPU-port banking.
Inputs: X selects the logical sprite descriptor at $0218,X; the caller entered with $01 decremented for RAM-under-KERNAL access.
Outputs: Sets bit 6 in $0218,X, increments $01 to restore the caller's banking state, and returns.
Assumptions: This entry is reached only from the empty/no-projectile slot path with one outstanding DEC $01.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, $0218,X, $01, and return-address stack bytes; X and Y are preserved.
Hardware changes: Restores CPU-port $01 banking by one increment; no VIC-II/CIA/SID register write.

Purpose: configure one slot of a composite actor sprite. Inputs: X and Y are part and slot indices and the current part record is valid. Outputs: slot pointer, position, attribute, image, and flip metadata are updated. Assumptions: indices lie within the compositor arrays. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite metadata and RAM only.

Purpose: consume and prepare the next component of a composite sprite definition. Inputs: $02/$03 definition pointer, Y record cursor, and X slot. Outputs: the part is decoded or configured and X and Y advance. Assumptions: the record uses the observed part terminator and encoding. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and part scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: decode a compressed 63-byte sprite and place its part. Inputs: X slot, Y record cursor, and valid compressed-stream context. Outputs: decoded cache and configured part slot are produced. Assumptions: the decoder pointer and part record are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C5/$C6, and decoder and compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: place an already decoded sprite part into the selected composite slot. Inputs: A is preserved across setup, $C5/$C6 hold saved X/Y, and ($02),Y addresses the part record. Outputs: position and attribute arrays are populated and the preserved A is restored by the shared tail. Assumptions: $C5/$C6 and the decoded buffer were prepared by the caller. Clobbers: X, Y, flags, and compositor scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: merge a sprite part into its composite destination under the current mask mode. Inputs: decoded source, destination pointer, placement and flip state, and mode $F1. Outputs: the 63-byte destination sprite region is updated. Assumptions: source and destination each cover the required 63 bytes. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and mask and pointer scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: select the backing buffer for a sprite slot. Inputs: X is sprite-slot index and slot flags are valid. Outputs: the destination pointer is installed in compositor zero page. Assumptions: X lies within the pointer tables. Clobbers: A, flags, and destination pointer; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: merge the cached decoded sprite mask into the active destination. Inputs: $02C0 cache, destination pointer, three masks, and mode $F1. Outputs: the transformed destination sprite bytes are updated. Assumptions: the cache contains a complete decoded sprite. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and mask scratch. Hardware changes: changes sprite RAM only.

Purpose: resolve and expand one tokenized sprite into the fixed 63-byte decode buffer, unless the alternate $C7 mode suppresses decoding
Inputs: A = sprite index; mode byte $C7; split source-pointer tables $B6C4/$B7C4 plus base $F6C4; token stream at resolved $06/$07
Outputs: normal mode fills exactly $02C0-$02FE and returns A=$FF, X=$3F; tokens $69-$6F emit zero runs and $68 escapes a literal; alternate $C7 bit-6 mode adjusts pointer state and returns A=0 without filling the buffer
Assumptions: the sprite index resolves to a valid terminated/length-bounded token stream
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, source pointer $06/$07, and decoder scratch
Hardware changes: none; writes only the 63-byte RAM sprite buffer

Expand a packed sprite into the 63-byte cache $02C0-$02FE from pointer $06/$07. Bytes $69-$6F emit 1-7 zeros; $68 escapes the following byte as one literal, including reserved values. Other bytes are literals. X counts output bytes; Y counts input bytes; return A=$FF. Every one of the 162 main-pool records expands to exactly 63 bytes and consumes precisely the distance to the next record.

Purpose: Resolve The Sewers playable phase's alternate raw sprite pointer without decoding the 63-byte cache.
Inputs: A is the encoded sprite selector and $06 contributes its carried high-address bit; $C7 bit 6 selected raw-pointer mode before this entry.
Outputs: Computes and stores the raw sprite pointer in $06/$07, returns A=0, preserves X, and leaves $02C0-$02FE unchanged.
Assumptions: The encoded selector maps to a valid raw sprite address in the active phase occupant.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, Z, C, and $06/$07; X and the 63-byte cache are preserved.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: update auxiliary sprite or object slot zero. Inputs: slot-zero state at $0280 and shared object and sprite state. Purpose: update auxiliary sprite or object slot one. Inputs: slot-one state and shared object and sprite state. Outputs: slot-one image and position state advance when active and eligible. Purpose: Render The Sewers playable phase's auxiliary/projectile sprite slot selected by Y through the common slot-1 body.

Assumptions: Y is 0 or 1 and the projectile sprite tables match the active phase.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $C5-$C7, sprite work buffers, and scene-condition scratch.
Hardware changes: Changes CPU-port $01 transiently within the composition helper and restores it before tail transfer; updates sprite work buffers but does not directly write VIC-II registers.

25-byte instruction continuation of $A7C4, including undocumented LAX absolute,Y at $A7D7. LAX loads both A/X from the $DC36+Y I/O address; SBC $0486 and CPX $04E4 select paths that execute optional BIT instructions. Every path reaches LDA #4 and stores four through both display pointers $7A/$86 at Y. Four native combinations of comparison operands/carry passed, and LAX A/X matched the stopped CIA timer value for Y=0. The comparisons change the path, not the stored value; exact raster timing and purpose of the comparisons remain open.
